products.name: Blue Prism
products.note: Enterprise RPA; digital workforce; centralized control; UK-hosted; GDPR relevant

reading.body:
SS&C Blue Prism positions itself as an orchestration layer for enterprise AI agents, combining rule-based automation with AI decision-making to run more complex workflows than traditional RPA alone.

The company's product stack reflects a shift in automation priorities. WorkHQ anchors the platform as an agentic automation system, while Chorus handles orchestration across the enterprise and the AI Gateway manages governance. This layering suggests the market now treats AI agent deployment as an operational infrastructure problem requiring not just execution capability but coordination and oversight across an organization. For enterprises running multiple AI agents, this addresses a genuine constraint: agents need to work together and be supervised.

The emphasis on governance, audit trails, and guardrails indicates that moving AI agents from prototype to production in regulated environments requires more than capability. UK hosting and GDPR relevance appear deliberate positioning for a market concerned with data residency and compliance. This does not tell a reader whether these governance features are substantively different from competitors or whether enterprises actually demand them more than they demand cost or performance.

The data does not capture market share, customer workloads, or whether agentic automation actually reduces compute or power consumption compared to alternatives. It also does not reveal whether this layer consumes significant infrastructure itself or merely manages consumption elsewhere.
